data.name: Aabdar
data.gender_notes: Aabdar is used as a male name in islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From Persian ābdār (آبدار) 'possessing water, lustrous, polished', from āb (آب) 'water' and the suffix -dār 'having, possessing'. It is used of gems and polished steel, hence the sense 'bright, shining, clear'. Aabdar therefore means “Lustrous; bright; polished; 'possessing water'”. Persian adjective ābdār 'lustrous, watered, polished'; used as a personal name in Persian/Urdu.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aabdar expresses “Servant of Allah”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.

faq.a: Aabdar is the Persian word ābdār, literally 'possessing water' (āb 'water' + -dār 'having'). Because water gives a bright, clear sheen, the word came to describe anything lustrous or polished - gems, steel and clear surfaces.

faq.q: What does the name Aabdar mean?
Where does the name Aabdar come from?
What is the linguistic root of Aabdar?
faq.a: The root of Aabdar is Persian ābdār (آبدار), from āb (آب) 'water' + -dār 'having'.

faq.q: How is Aabdar written in Arabic script?
faq.a: Aabdar is written آبدار in Arabic script.

faq.q: Is Aabdar a boy's or a girl's name?
faq.a: Aabdar is used as a male name.

faq.q: Does Aabdar appear in the Qur'an?
faq.a: No. Aabdar is not a Qur'anic name; it is used in Muslim naming tradition.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Aabdar verified?
faq.a: Yes — the meaning “Lustrous; bright; polished; 'possessing water'” is established by Persian adjective ābdār 'lustrous, watered, polished'; used as a personal name in Persian/Urdu..
